حسابك على Door43 ليس ضمن قائمة المحرِّرين بعد. اطلب من مسؤول إضافتك. وإن كنت قد استخدمت الحساب الخطأ فاختر **تسجيل الدخول بحساب Door43 آخر**. انظر [البدء](#help:getting-started).

## كيف أغيّر لغة القوائم؟
افتح قائمة حسابك (الزر الدائري في أعلى جهة النهاية) واختر **لغة الواجهة**. هذا يغيّر الأزرار والقوائم، لا النص الذي تترجمه. انظر [البدء](#help:getting-started).

## يظهر على سفر «غير مستورد» ولا أستطيع فتحه. لماذا؟
يجب أن يُحضر المسؤول السفر إلى التطبيق أولًا. اطلب من المسؤول فتح **الأسفار** واختيار السفر ثم **إحضار**. انظر [الأسفار](#help:books).

## كتبت ملاحظة لكن الشريط العلوي يقول «غير محفوظ». هل ضاع عملي؟
لا. نصك محفوظ في متصفحك، ويعود عندما ترجع إلى تلك الملاحظة. اختر **حفظ** (أو **حفظ واعتماد**) لإرساله. انظر [الحفظ والعمل دون اتصال](#help:save-and-sync).

## هل تذهب تعديلاتي مباشرة إلى Door43؟
لا. تذهب أولًا إلى قاعدة بيانات التطبيق نفسه. ومرة كل ليلة ينشر التطبيق المحتوى المعتمد على Door43. انظر [الحفظ والعمل دون اتصال](#help:save-and-sync).

## ماذا يحدث إذا انقطع اتصالي بالإنترنت؟
تابع العمل. كل تعديل تحفظه ينتظر في قائمة انتظار في متصفحك ويُرسل عندما يعود الاتصال. انظر [الحفظ والعمل دون اتصال](#help:save-and-sync).

## حرّر شخص آخر الملاحظة نفسها. ماذا أفعل الآن؟
لا يكتب التطبيق فوق عمله. يخبرك شريط أو نافذة بذلك، وتختار كيف تحتفظ بنسختك أو تحمّل نسخته. انظر [الحفظ والعمل دون اتصال](#help:save-and-sync).

## ماذا يفعل الاعتماد؟
الاعتماد يضع على ملاحظة أو سؤال أو آية علامة أنها منتهية ومراجَعة. لا ينشر Door43 إلا الملاحظات والأسئلة المعتمدة. انظر [الملاحظات](#help:notes).

## كيف أحصل على مسودة ذكاء اصطناعي جديدة لملاحظة؟
في شاشة الملاحظات اختر **إعادة الصياغة**. يعمل الذكاء الاصطناعي في الخلفية وتظهر المسودة الجديدة عندما تصبح جاهزة. انظر [الملاحظات](#help:notes).

## أصبحت بعض الكلمات في آيتي «غير مُحاذاة». لماذا؟
تغيير الكلمات في آية قد يزيل ارتباطها بكلمات الأصل. افتح شاشة المحاذاة واربطها من جديد. انظر [محاذاة الكلمات](#help:alignment).

## كيف أرى العبرية أو اليونانية وراء كلمة؟
افتح عرض الآية وانقر الكلمة. تعرض اللوحة الكلمة الأصلية ومدخلها في المعجم. انظر [عرض الآية](#help:verse-view).

## أين المحرر القديم ذو الأعمدة الثلاثة؟
افتح قائمة حسابك واختر **المحرر الكلاسيكي**. انظر [المحرر الكلاسيكي](#help:classic-editor).

## كيف أضيف شخصًا إلى فريقي؟
يفعل المسؤولون ذلك في منطقة المسؤول. انظر [الفريق](#help:admin-team).

articles.title: Getting started
headings: If you are not allowed in
articles.body:
BPtranslate is a web app where your team translates scripture and the translation helps. You sign in with your Door43 account. This page covers signing in, the top bar, and the settings you reach from your account button.

![The Books screen with the top bar and the account button at the top right](/help/en/books-1.png)

## Sign in
1. Open the app. If you are not signed in, you see **Sign in to continue**.
2. Select **Sign in with Door43**.
3. Door43 asks you to approve the sign-in. After you approve, you come back to the app. The first screen is **Books**.

If you signed out earlier, the screen says **You're signed out**. Edits you had queued stay in your browser until you sign in again.

## If you are not allowed in
After you sign in, you may see **Not authorized**. It says your Door43 account is not on the editor list for this app (or for the organization's workspace). Ask an admin to add you. Then select **Sign in with a different Door43 account** if you used the wrong account. Door43 may remember the old account, so sign out of Door43 itself first.

Some people can only read. You then see a banner at the top: you are signed in as a member with read-only access, and edits will not be saved. Ask an admin to add you as an editor if you need to edit.

## The top bar
Every screen has one bar at the top. The screen name and a back arrow are on the left. On the right you see:

- A save status: **saved**, **saving**, **offline**, or **N unsaved**. See [Saving and working offline](#help:save-and-sync).
- A round button with the first letter of your user name. This is your account menu.
- A **?** button that opens this guide.

If a newer version of the app is available, a button **App update available — refresh** appears. Save your work first, then select it.

## Your account menu
Select the round button. The menu shows your user name and organization, and these items:

- **Start an AI run** (**Import from Door43** in a source project): on a phone only, and only for editors and admins, on a book's package and on the Scripture, Notes and Questions screens. It is first in the menu. On a wider screen it is an icon in the top bar instead. See [Translating scripture](#help:scripture).
- **Organization**: switch organization. It appears only if you belong to more than one. Switching reloads the app, and it is blocked while unsaved edits are still syncing.
- **Switch to dark mode**.
- **Interface language**: choose the language of menus and buttons. Arabic, Persian and Urdu switch the screen to right-to-left. This does not change the text you translate.
- **Reading text size**: make the text smaller or larger.
- **Classic editor**: see [Classic editor](#help:classic-editor).
- **Admin**: admins only.
- **Sign out**.

If your Door43 account belongs to several organizations, a **Choose your organization** window may open after sign-in. Pick one, or select **Continue** to stay where you are.

## Getting help
Select the **?** button in the top bar to open this guide. On a phone, open your account menu (the round button) and select **Help**; in the classic editor it is in the **More** menu. It opens on the page for the screen you are on. Type in **Search help** to find a topic.

If your admin has turned it on, the guide also has an **Ask AI** area at the bottom. Type a question and the app first shows up to three topics that may answer it under **Did one of these answer it?**. If none does, select **Ask AI**. The answer comes from this guide, and the topics it used appear under **From the guide:**. You can ask follow-up questions, or select **New question** to start over. Each person has a daily allowance, and the area shows how much is **left today**. When the allowance is used up, it says when it resets. Searching the guide always works.

## Next
Go to [Books](#help:books) to open a book.

articles.title: Books and the book package
articles.body:
The **Books** screen is the first screen of the app. It lists all 66 books. Pick a book to open its package, which is the place that leads to every kind of work on that book.

![The Books screen with the book list and the details of Obadiah](/help/en/books-1.png)

## Open a book
1. Find the book. You can scroll the Old and New Testament lists, or type in **Search books…**.
2. Each book shows **Imported** or **Not imported**. Only imported books can be opened.
3. Select the book. The details appear next to the list (below it on a phone). They show how many chapters, notes and questions are loaded.
4. Select **Open OBA** (with your book's code). This opens the book package.

If a book is not imported, you see **Nothing to open yet — an administrator brings books into the editor.**

## Continue where you stopped
When you have worked before, a **CONTINUE** card at the top shows the last place you were, for example Obadiah 1:1. Select **Open OBA** to go to that book's package. Select **Notes** to jump to the notes for that verse.

## Bring in a book (admins)
Admins see an **Import** heading and an extra panel for each book.
1. Select a book that is **Not imported**.
2. Select **Bring in OBA…**.
3. Under **Intent**, choose **Translate a new book** (loads the English source text, notes and questions for you to translate) or **Load my existing work** (loads the book from your organization's own repository).
4. For most books, leave the sources on the default and select **Bring in OBA**.

A large book can take up to a minute. If you leave the screen, the import still runs. For a book that is already imported, **Re-pull…** fetches fresh content from Door43 without replacing rows that translators already edited. A forced re-import that throws away edits asks you to confirm first.

## The book package
After **Open**, you see the package for the book. The back arrow returns to **Books**.

![The package for Obadiah with the lifecycle card and the work rows](/help/en/books-2.png)

- **Book lifecycle** shows progress: **Notes approved**, **Questions approved** and **Verses done**. Admins also see **Publish this book** and **Latest publish results**. Publishing sends approved content to Door43. Rows still waiting for review are held back.
- **Chapter by chapter**: **Scripture**, **Notes**, **Questions** and **Alignment**. Select a row to open its chapter list, then choose a chapter. A row with nothing in it (for example no notes) is greyed out.
- **Whole book**: **Verse view** and **Words & Articles**.

Editors and admins also have an icon in the package's top bar. In a translation project it is a sparkle icon, **Start an AI run**, with **Translate chapter**, **Translate questions** and **Import from Door43** (admins also see **Pull Aquifer drafts** and **Re-source notes from English**). In a source project it is a download icon, **Import from Door43**. On a phone it is the first item in your account menu instead. The Scripture, Notes and Questions screens have the same icon; [Translating scripture](#help:scripture) explains what each item does.

Related: [Scripture](#help:scripture), [Notes](#help:notes), [Questions](#help:questions), [Alignment](#help:alignment), [Verse view](#help:verse-view), [Words and articles](#help:words).

articles.title: Translating scripture
articles.body:
The **Scripture** screen is where you write and approve the verses of one chapter, one verse at a time. Each verse has two boxes, one for each of your project's two texts. They carry your project's own names, for example **GLT** and **GST**, or **AVD** and **NAV**. In unfoldingWord's English source these are the ULT (the literal text, which follows the original words closely) and the UST (the simplified text, which says the meaning in plain words). In a translation project, both boxes hold your own language.

![The Scripture screen at Obadiah 1:1 with the verse list and the two text boxes](/help/en/scripture-1.png)

## Open the screen
1. Open a book from [Books](#help:books).
2. In the package, select **Scripture**, then choose a chapter.

The title shows the book and chapter, for example `OBA 1`. Next to it you see **Verse 1 of 21** and the arrows **Previous verse** and **Next verse**. A thin bar shows how far you have come.

On a wide screen, the list of verses is on the left. Each verse can show a chip: **Approved** or **Draft saved**. On a phone you see one verse at a time. You can also swipe sideways to move to the next or previous verse (not when you start in a text box).

![The same screen on a phone](/help/en/scripture-phone.png)

## Write a verse
1. Read the reference card. It shows the verse and the original-language text.
2. Click in the first of the two boxes (**Your text** followed by your project's first text name, for example **Your text · GLT**) and write or correct the verse. Do the same in the second box (for example **Your text · GST**).
3. Select **Save draft** to save both boxes without approving. A message **Draft saved** appears.
4. When the verse is finished, select **Approve verse**. It saves both boxes and marks the verse done.
5. Select **Next** to go to the next verse.

Each box has a chip: **Imported** (nobody changed it), **Edited**, or **Approved**.

## When you finish a chapter
After the last verse, you see **OBA 1 scripture complete** with the number of verses approved. Select **Continue to OBA 2** or **Review again**.

## Alignment
Alignment connects your words to the original words. Editing a verse keeps the alignment of the words you did not touch. If a save would remove the alignment of words you did not change, a window **This save would unalign words it didn't touch** lists them. Choose **Cancel** to go back, or **Save anyway**. Your typing is kept either way. Fix the unaligned words afterwards.

On a wide screen, each box has an **Align** button. **Align both** opens both texts side by side. Both open the [Alignment](#help:alignment) screen.

## Start an AI run
Editors and admins have one more icon in the top bar.

In a translation project it is a sparkle icon, **Start an AI run**. It opens a menu:
- **Translate chapter**: the AI drafts the chapter's translation notes.
- **Translate questions**: the AI drafts the chapter's translation questions.
- **Import from Door43**: opens its own window. Type a chapter or a range under **Chapter or range**, tick what to bring in under **What to import:**, and press **Import**. Rows that translators already edited are skipped.
- **Pull Aquifer drafts** (admins only): starts at once for the whole book, with no confirm window. It adds Aquifer translation notes as drafts to review, and it marks the notes that are already translated as approved.
- **Re-source notes from English** (admins only): re-downloads the whole book from Door43: the scripture from your project's own Bible text (or from the English source if your project has none for this book), and the notes, questions and word links from the English source. Local edits to the book are lost. Press **Re-source** to confirm. If the book has local edits, a second window counts them and asks again: **Discard and re-source**.

After **Translate chapter** or **Translate questions**, a confirm window opens: type a chapter or a range under **Chapter or range** and press **Start**.

In a source project, one that does not translate from another language (such as unfoldingWord's English), the icon is a download icon, **Import from Door43**. It opens the import window straight away, with no menu.

On a phone the icon is not in the top bar. It is the first item in your account menu, with the same name.

While a **Translate chapter** or **Translate questions** run is starting, running or paused on a chapter, that chapter's verses can't be saved. A run that is still waiting in line locks nothing. Admins follow the runs in [AI studio](#help:admin-ai).

## Good to know
- If you only have view access, you see a notice and the boxes are read-only.
- While an AI run is rewriting the chapter, a save can be refused and dropped instead of overwriting. The screen then tells you the verse was not approved.
- If someone else changed the verse, a message tells you to resolve the conflict from the status bar. See [Saving and working offline](#help:save-and-sync).

articles.title: Verse view
articles.body:
The **Verse view** helps you check one verse. It shows the original text (Hebrew or Greek), the literal text (ULT) and the simplified text (UST) joined on the same words. If you click a word in one text, the same place lights up in the other two. **Nothing on this screen changes your work.** It is for reading and checking.

![The Verse view at Obadiah 1:1 in Read mode with the detail panel](/help/en/verse-view-1.png)

## Open it
1. Open a book from [Books](#help:books).
2. In the package, under **Whole book**, select **Verse view**. It opens at the last verse you worked on in that book, or at 1:1.

The back arrow returns to the package.

## Move between verses
- Select **Previous verse** or **Next verse**. The arrow keys (← →) do the same.
- Use **Go to verse** to jump to a verse in the same chapter.
- The count, for example **Verse 1 of 21**, shows where you are.

## Scroll through the chapter
Choose **Scroll** at the top (next to **One verse**) to see the whole chapter as one list, verse after verse. Scroll with the mouse wheel, the trackpad or your finger.

- Each verse keeps everything it has in **One verse**: the three texts, its checks, and its notes, word links and questions.
- The count, **Go to verse** and the arrows follow the verse at the top of the list. The arrows and **Go to verse** move the list to the verse you pick.
- Select a word in any verse. On a wide screen the detail panel shows it. On a narrow screen the detail appears under that verse's text.
- The address in the browser follows the verse you are reading, so a reload or a bookmark opens at that verse.
- After the last verse, select **Continue to chapter** to go on to the next chapter, still in **Scroll**. The book's last chapter has no such button.

Your choice is remembered on this device. Choose **One verse** to go back to one verse at a time, at the verse you were reading.

## Read mode and Audit mode
At the top, choose **Read** or **Audit**.

- **Read** shows the verse three ways: **Original**, **Literal** and **Simplified**. Click any word to see what the other texts do with it.
- **Audit** shows one row for each original word. Each row shows what the literal text made of that word and what the simplified text made of it. A word that a text does not translate shows **not rendered**. This is often correct, so treat it as a question, not an error. Words added with no original word behind them are listed under the rows.

## The detail panel
Select a word, a row, a note or a word link. The panel (below the text on a narrow screen) shows:

- the original word with its grammar and its lexicon entry;
- the literal and simplified text for that word;
- the notes and word links that attach to it.

The resources of the verse are listed in groups: **Notes**, **Word links** and **Questions**, each with a count. Select one to see it in the panel. A note whose quote does not match the original text of this verse is marked **quote not anchored**.

## Read a helps article
When you select a note or a word link, the panel can show **Read the translationAcademy article →** or **Read the translationWords article →**. The article opens in place. Select **Back to the list** to return, or **Open in the article editor** to go to the full article. See [Words and articles](#help:words).

If a book has no original text loaded, the screen says so and still lists the resources.

articles.title: Word alignment
articles.body:
**What is word alignment?** Alignment links each word in your translation to the word or words in the original Hebrew or Greek that it translates. These links let the other tools show which note belongs to which words, and let a reader see where a word comes from. A word with no link is **unaligned**. Alignment is saved with the verse.

![The Alignment screen at Obadiah 1:1 with the verse list and the aligner](/help/en/alignment-1.png)

## Open the screen
- From the package, select **Alignment** and choose a chapter. Or:
- On the [Scripture](#help:scripture) screen, select **Align** (one text) or **Align both** (both texts).

The title is **Alignment**. Under it you see the book and chapter and an arrow from the original text to the text you are aligning, for example `OBA 1 · UHB → ULT`. The count **N of M fully aligned** shows the progress of the chapter. The verse list has a chip for each verse: **Aligned**, **N unaligned**, **Source gaps** (original words with nothing linked to them) or **Not drafted**.

## Single or dual
Two buttons choose the view:

- **Single** aligns one text at a time. Choose which one with the text picker next to it (it lists your project's two text names, for example GLT or GST).
- **Dual** puts your project's two texts (for example GLT and GST) side by side in a full-screen window. Both are aligned to the same original words, so you can compare them. Dual is greyed out if the verse has no text to compare.

![Dual mode with the project's two texts side by side](/help/en/alignment-2.png)

In Dual mode you can also correct the verse text. Save the alignment first, then edit. When you close with unsaved work, the window **Unsaved changes** offers **Cancel**, **Discard** or **Save**.

## Align the words (Single)
The screen offers two ways to work. On a large screen you can switch between **Drag canvas** and **Tap mode**. On a phone only Tap mode is available.

Drag canvas:
1. Drag a word chip from the word bank onto a card of original words (**drop English here**).
2. To split a joined original group, double-click the original word. To unalign a word, double-click it or drag it back to the word bank.
3. Select **Save** followed by the text name, for example **Save GLT** (the button names the text you are aligning). **Reset** returns to the last saved version.

Tap mode:
1. Tap a card of original words, then tap the target words that belong to it. (Or tap target words first, then the card.)
2. If suggestions are shown, select **✓ Accept** or **✗ Skip** for each one.
3. Use **Unalign**, **Combine** or **Split** to fix a pairing.
4. Select **Save alignment**. You can see **N of M words aligned** and use **Jump to unaligned** to find what is left.

## Good to know
- If you have view-only access, alignment is read-only.
- Before you switch text or mode, save or reset your unsaved alignment. The switch is blocked until then.
- If a save would unalign words you did not touch, a window asks you to confirm.

articles.title: Translating notes
articles.body:
The **Translation Notes** screen is where you translate the notes (tN) of one chapter. A translation note explains a hard place in a verse. Each note has a quote from the original text, a link to a translationAcademy (tA) article, and the note text. You see the English note and write your own version next to it.

![The Translation Notes screen at Obadiah 1:1 with the note list and the draft](/help/en/notes-1.png)

## Open the screen
1. Open a book from [Books](#help:books).
2. In the package, select **Notes**, then choose a chapter. Or select **Notes** on the **CONTINUE** card to jump to the note at your last verse.

The header shows the book and chapter. A count such as **1 of 5** shows where you are. Use the arrows or **Next** and **Previous** to move. On a wide screen the list of notes is on the left. Each row has a verse, a preview and a status chip: **Draft**, **Edited**, **Pending**, **Unsaved** or **Approved**. If the chapter has many kinds of notes, a menu with **All types** filters by tA article type.

## Translate one note
The note appears as a stack of cards:
1. The original-language quote the note is about.
2. The scripture card with the verse. The words of the quote are highlighted. When it is available, chips above the verse let you show the English ULT text and its alignment.
3. The **English note** (read-only).
4. Your draft, titled with your language, for example **Draft** or **draft · AI** when an AI wrote it.

To write your note:
1. Click the text of your draft. A box opens.
2. Type or correct the note.
3. Select **Save** to keep your text without approving it.
4. When it is right, select **Save & Approve** at the bottom. This saves and marks the note approved.

The other two buttons at the bottom:
- **Redo** asks the AI for a fresh draft. It works in the background and the new draft appears when ready. It needs a quote and a support reference on the note.
- **Not needed** sets the note aside when it does not need translating. It goes to the trash. Until the nightly publish you can bring it back in the [Review queue](#help:review-queue). After that it is deleted for good. If someone else changed the note and your screen does not show their change yet, it is not set aside: the app reloads it and tells you, so you can read their change first.

An icon next to the verse opens the verse view. See [Verse view](#help:verse-view).

## Rapid check
On a screen at least 1200 pixels wide, such as most laptops, the **Rapid check** button in the top bar switches to a compact list for checking many notes quickly. Select it again to go back to the cards. The app remembers your choice in this browser. On a smaller screen or a narrow window you always see the cards, and the button is hidden.

![Rapid check at Obadiah 1:3: the verse at the top and its notes as rows](/help/en/notes-rapid.png)

The verse stays at the top while you scroll, one short line per scripture text. Below it, each note of the verse is one row: its status, its tA type, the original-language quote, the **English note**, and your note. Choose a type under **All types**, on the verse's top line, to list every note of that type in the chapter instead, grouped by verse.

To hide notes by status, press **Filter by status** (the funnel beside **Status · type** in the column header). Untick a status to hide it, for example **Approved**, or press **Only** beside one status to see just those notes. The list then shows every matching note in the chapter, grouped by verse, and a line above the columns says what is hidden; **Show all** brings everything back. The note you have open stays in the list while it is open, so approving it does not make it jump away; it leaves the list when you move on. If a new choice hides the open note, the next shown note opens instead. The filter works together with a type filter and stays on when you change chapters.

**Verse: Top | Inline**, on the same line, chooses where the scripture lines show. With **Top** (the usual setting), the open note's verse stays at the top, as described above. With **Inline**, the top keeps only its buttons, and each verse's scripture lines sit right above that verse's notes and scroll with them. With a type filter, every verse group starts with its own scripture lines, with the quotes of the listed notes highlighted. The app remembers your choice in this browser, and **V** switches between the two. A text you hide with its short name is hidden in either place.

- Click your note in any row to edit it. Select **Save** to keep it, or **Save & Approve** at the bottom to save and approve it. Click anywhere else in a row to make it the current note without editing.
- In the editor, **Close** (or **Esc**) closes it and keeps what you typed as an unsaved draft. **Discard changes**, shown once you have changed the note, puts back the saved text and closes the editor.
- The circle after a row's checkbox approves that note. It fills in when the note is approved. A note with unsaved typing has to be opened and saved first.
- Click a filled circle to take the approval back. The note shows **Pending** again and a message says **Approval removed**. Click the circle again to approve it.
- The pencil next to the current note's quote opens the quote picker, where you choose which original-language words the note is about. When the original-language column is hidden, **Q** still opens the picker.
- To move to another verse, use the arrows on either side of the reference at the top, or select the reference to pick a verse from the list. The list shows only verses that have notes, with how many each has.
- The short names at the end of the verse's top line, such as **ULT** and **UST**, show or hide each scripture text. A name stays there while its text is hidden, so you can always bring it back.
- To make room for your note, hide the original-language column or the **English note** column with the crossed-out eye in its heading. A hidden column becomes a small **+** button at the end of the headings: select it to bring the column back.
- The app remembers which texts and columns you hid, in this browser, for every book.

Keys work once you click a blank part of the list or a note's type:
- **J** and **K** (or the arrow keys) move to the next and previous note.
- **[** and **]** move to the previous and next verse.
- **Enter** opens the editor. Inside it, **Ctrl+Enter** saves and approves, and **Esc** closes it. What you typed is kept.
- **A** approves the current note, saving it first if you changed it, and moves on.
- **E** shows or hides the English column. **U** shows or hides the English ULT, when the screen offers it.
- **Q** opens the quote picker for the current note. **Esc** closes it.
- **V** switches the verse between the top and inline.
- The keyboard button at the start of the column headings lists these keys.

### Check several notes at once
Each row starts with a checkbox. Checked notes get a bar at the bottom in place of the usual buttons:
- Click a checkbox to check one note. Hold **Shift** and click another to check every note in between. The checkbox above the list checks or clears every note shown.
- With the keyboard, **Space** or **X** checks the current note, and **Shift+J** or **Shift+K** checks the next or previous note too.
- **Approve** approves the checked notes. If the open note is checked and has a change, it is saved first.
- **Redo with AI** asks the AI for new drafts of the checked notes in one run, from the English notes, so it is offered only in a translation workspace. Those notes are read-only until it finishes.
- **Not needed** sets the checked notes aside. Select **Undo** in the message that appears, or press **Ctrl+Z**, to bring them back.

The app skips a note, and tells you how many it skipped and why, when it has unsaved typing, a change still saving, or someone else changed it since you loaded it. **Redo with AI** also skips approved notes. Skipped notes stay checked. Approving has no Undo.

### Ask the assistant
The **Assistant** button, under the list, opens a chat beside it. Ask in your own words for a change to the notes, for example to use one spelling of a name in the checked notes. It sees the notes of the chapter you have open, and which ones you checked. Ask about the checked notes to keep the answer small.

Nothing changes until you press **Apply**:
- The assistant answers, and may add a list of proposed changes. Each edit is shown as the note with the changed words marked. Words it would remove are struck through and words it would add are highlighted.
- Every proposed edit, approval and **Not needed** has a checkbox. Untick any you do not want, then press **Apply** with the number of changes left.
- Edited notes become **Edited** and still need your approval. The assistant can also propose approving or setting aside notes, but a note it edits is never approved in the same step.
- The app skips a note, and tells you how many it skipped and why, when it has unsaved typing, a change still saving, or the note changed since the assistant looked. A proposed edit, approval or **Not needed** is also skipped when the note was approved or un-approved since then, and a proposed edit is skipped when the note was set aside or changed in another way that this screen had not shown yet. For these the result gives the reason as changed since the proposal. Skipped notes are not changed.
- An edit that has not finished saving when the result appears is reported as **Still saving**. It may still save, so check the note before you ask for the change again.

Each person can use the assistant up to a daily dollar amount, shown under the box. When it is used up, it comes back the next day. A chat has a length limit, so start a **New chat** when it is full or you change topic. If the assistant says the request was too big, ask about fewer notes. A line under the reply says how many notes were not sent, either because they are too long or because the chapter has too many for one request; in the second case, check only the notes you mean so they are sent first. The Assistant button appears only when an admin has turned it on under **AI service**, and only for editors and admins.

## When you finish a chapter
You see **OBA 1 notes complete** with a count of approved, edited and not-needed notes. Select **Continue to chapter 2** or **Review again**.

## Start an AI run
Editors and admins have one more icon in the top bar.

In a translation project it is a sparkle icon, **Start an AI run**. It opens a menu:
- **Translate chapter**: the AI drafts the chapter's translation notes.
- **Translate questions**: the AI drafts the chapter's translation questions.
- **Import from Door43**: opens its own window. Type a chapter or a range under **Chapter or range**, tick what to bring in under **What to import:**, and press **Import**. Rows that translators already edited are skipped.
- **Pull Aquifer drafts** (admins only): starts at once for the whole book, with no confirm window. It adds Aquifer translation notes as drafts to review, and it marks the notes that are already translated as approved.
- **Re-source notes from English** (admins only): re-downloads the whole book from Door43: the scripture from your project's own Bible text (or from the English source if your project has none for this book), and the notes, questions and word links from the English source. Local edits to the book are lost. Press **Re-source** to confirm. If the book has local edits, a second window counts them and asks again: **Discard and re-source**.

After **Translate chapter** or **Translate questions**, a confirm window opens: type a chapter or a range under **Chapter or range** and press **Start**.

A **Translate chapter** run does not redraft notes that are already approved. It keeps them as they are, and when the run ends a banner lists them. To get a new AI draft for an approved note, use **Redo** on that note. If the AI returns a note unchanged from the English, that draft is not applied: the note keeps its text, and a banner lists it.

In a source project, one that does not translate from another language (such as unfoldingWord's English), the icon is a download icon, **Import from Door43**. It opens the import window straight away, with no menu.

On a phone the icon is not in the top bar. It is the first item in your account menu, with the same name.

While a **Translate chapter** run is starting, running or paused on a chapter, that chapter's notes can't be saved. During a **Translate questions** run you can still edit and remove existing notes, but you can't add one. A run that is still waiting in line locks nothing. Admins follow the runs in [AI studio](#help:admin-ai).

## Good to know
- Your text is kept in your browser while you type. The top bar shows **N unsaved** until you save. See [Saving and working offline](#help:save-and-sync).
- If another editor saved the same note first, a banner says your version was not saved. Select **Reload note** to see their version.
- Only approved notes are published to Door43. Draft and edited notes keep their last published text.
- If you only have view access, you can read but not edit.

articles.title: Translating questions
articles.body:
The **Translation Questions** screen is where you translate the questions (tQ) of one chapter. A translation question checks that the reader understood a verse. Each one has a **Question** and an **Expected answer**. You see the English text and write the same thing in your language.

![The Translation Questions screen at Obadiah 1:1 with the question list and the two fields](/help/en/questions-1.png)

## Open the screen
1. Open a book from [Books](#help:books).
2. In the package, select **Questions**, then choose a chapter. The row is greyed out if the book has no questions.

The header shows the book and chapter and a count such as **1 of 5**. Use the arrows or **Next** and **Previous** to move. On a wide screen the list of questions is on the left, with a verse, a preview and a status chip on each row.

## Translate one question
Each question is a stack of cards:
1. The reference and the verse in ULT and UST (the literal and the simplified text).
2. **Question**: the English question, then your box.
3. **Expected answer**: the English answer, then your box.

To write:
1. Click the text of your question. A box opens. Type or correct it.
2. Do the same for the **Expected answer**.
3. Select **Save** to keep your text without approving it.
4. When both are right, select **Save & Approve** at the bottom.

There is only one decision here: **Save & Approve**. Questions are changed, not skipped. If you do not like a question, edit it and approve your version. There is also no **Redo** button on this screen. A chip shows the state of the row: **Draft**, **Edited**, **Approved** or **Unsaved**.

If the English source for a question is not available, the screen says so. This can happen for a question that was added in this project and not translated from the published questions.

## When you finish a chapter
You see **OBA 1 questions reviewed**, with a count of questions **Approved as-is**, **Edited** and the **Total**. Select **Continue to chapter 2** or **Review again**.

## Start an AI run
Editors and admins have one more icon in the top bar.

In a translation project it is a sparkle icon, **Start an AI run**. It opens a menu:
- **Translate chapter**: the AI drafts the chapter's translation notes.
- **Translate questions**: the AI drafts the chapter's translation questions.
- **Import from Door43**: opens its own window. Type a chapter or a range under **Chapter or range**, tick what to bring in under **What to import:**, and press **Import**. Rows that translators already edited are skipped.
- **Pull Aquifer drafts** (admins only): starts at once for the whole book, with no confirm window. It adds Aquifer translation notes as drafts to review, and it marks the notes that are already translated as approved.
- **Re-source notes from English** (admins only): re-downloads the whole book from Door43: the scripture from your project's own Bible text (or from the English source if your project has none for this book), and the notes, questions and word links from the English source. Local edits to the book are lost. Press **Re-source** to confirm. If the book has local edits, a second window counts them and asks again: **Discard and re-source**.

After **Translate chapter** or **Translate questions**, a confirm window opens: type a chapter or a range under **Chapter or range** and press **Start**.

A **Translate questions** run does not redraft questions that are already approved. It keeps them as they are, and when the run ends a banner lists them. To get a new AI draft for an approved question, run the AI on that question alone.

In a source project, one that does not translate from another language (such as unfoldingWord's English), the icon is a download icon, **Import from Door43**. It opens the import window straight away, with no menu.

On a phone the icon is not in the top bar. It is the first item in your account menu, with the same name.

While any AI run is starting, running or paused on a chapter, that chapter's questions can't be saved or approved. A run that is still waiting in line locks nothing. Admins follow the runs in [AI studio](#help:admin-ai).

## Good to know
- Your typing is kept in your browser until you select **Save**. The top bar shows **N unsaved**. See [Saving and working offline](#help:save-and-sync).
- If an AI run is rewriting the chapter, a save is refused. The screen says your edit was dropped. **Save & Approve** is refused too, and the screen says the questions can't be approved yet. Try again when the run ends.
- If another editor saved the question first, a banner says your version was not saved. Select **Reload question**.
- If you only have view access, you can read the questions but not edit them.

articles.title: Words and articles
articles.body:
Two kinds of helps articles go with every book. **translationWords (tW)** explains key terms and names, such as "covenant". **translationAcademy (tA)** teaches translation principles, such as how to handle a metaphor. This guide covers two screens: **Words & Articles**, where you translate the articles a book uses, and the **Articles** screen, where you can read and edit any article.

![The Words & Articles screen for Obadiah](/help/en/words-1.png)

Article translation is only for projects that translate from a gateway language. Other projects see a message that it does not apply.

## Words & Articles
1. Open a book from [Books](#help:books).
2. In the package, under **Whole book**, select **Words & Articles**.

The list has two parts: **Words** and **Academy articles**. The words are in groups: **Key terms**, **Names** and **Other**. Each group shows how many articles are approved, for example **3 of 10 approved**. Inside a group, the articles used most in this book come first. Each row shows how often it is used (**N occurrences in OBA**, or **linked from N notes in OBA**) and a chip: **Not started**, **AI draft**, **Edited** or **Approved**.

An article that says **source not populated in this workspace** has no text to translate yet. An admin can fill it from the Articles screen.

## Translate an article
1. Select an article. On a wide screen it opens beside the list. On a phone, **Back to the list** returns you.
2. Choose how to read it: **Source**, **Target** or **Both**.
3. Click the target text to edit. A tA article has three parts, **Title**, **Subtitle** and **Article**. Sections are shown in pairs for reading, but tapping a section edits that whole part, and the parts are saved together.
4. Select **Done** when you finish typing. Then select **Save**.
5. Select **Approve** to save and approve. It needs a draft first. **Redo** asks the AI for a new draft, which arrives in the background.

If someone else saved a part first, a message says your text is still there and that saving again will work.

## The Articles screen
This screen shows one article at a time with a list on the left. You get here from a link in a note (the support reference), from **Open in the article editor** in the [Verse view](#help:verse-view), or from the classic editor menu **More**, under **Articles**.

![The Articles screen with the tW and tA lists](/help/en/words-2.png)

- Choose **Translation Words** or **Translation Academy**. Type in **Search articles** to find one. The list shows **N/M approved**.
- Select an article. Use **Edit** and **Preview** to switch between typing and a formatted view. Select **show source** to read the English.
- **Save** keeps your text. **Approve** approves it (**Un-approve** takes it back). **Translate** or **Re-run AI** asks the AI for a draft.
- A mark on a list item means unsaved changes.
- If the list is empty, **Populate from imported books** fills it with the articles that your books use.
- **Back to scripture** returns to where you were.

Your typing is kept in the browser until you save. See [Saving and working offline](#help:save-and-sync).

articles.title: Classic editor
articles.body:
The **Classic editor** shows a whole chapter at once: the verses, and all the helps for the active verse, in three columns. Use it when you want to see scripture, notes, word links and questions together, or to edit word links (TWLinks), which are edited in this editor. For translating one note or one question at a time, the [Notes](#help:notes) and [Questions](#help:questions) screens are simpler.

![The classic editor at Obadiah 1:1 with the verse rail, the scripture and the resources](/help/en/classic-editor-1.png)

## Open it
- Open your account menu (the round button in the top bar) and select **Classic editor**. It opens the book you were on, at your last verse.
- Or type the address `#/OBA/1/1` (book, chapter, verse) after the app's address.

## The three columns
1. **Verse rail** (left). One tile per verse. Select a tile to make that verse active. **hide verse list** and **show verse list** in the top bar hide and show this rail. The tiles show a mark for each kind of work (text, notes, TWLinks, questions). The **Board** button above them opens the chapter checkoff board, where you mark which parts of each verse you have checked.
2. **Scripture** (middle). The text of the chapter in each version. A control for the scripture view mode switches between **rows** (verse by verse, the default), **columns** (a side-by-side view of the chapter) and **book** (the whole book, loaded as you scroll). Use **find** (Ctrl+F) to find and replace in the chapter. **go to active** scrolls back to the active verse.
3. **Resources** (right). Tabs for **Notes**, **Questions**, **TWLinks**, **Alignment** and **Web Search (external)**. The web search is a third-party tool, and what you type there leaves the app.

On a narrow screen the columns are shown one at a time.

## Edit a verse
1. Click in the verse text and type.
2. Select **save edits**. Nothing is saved until you do. **undo edits to this verse** reverts your unsaved change.
3. Use the version history button to view or restore an earlier save.

Notes work the same way: edit the note, then save it. A note card also has a button to discard unsaved edits. Your typing is kept in the browser until you save. See [Saving and working offline](#help:save-and-sync).

## The top bar
- A book picker, chapter arrows (**previous chapter**, **next chapter**) and a **go to ref** box. Type `5`, `5:5`, `oba 1:5` or `ps 1:4` and press Enter.
- The save status, the AI run menu (in a source project, an **Import** button that opens **Import from Door43**) and **Layouts**, which switch between arrangements of the three columns.
- **More**: **Import from Door43** and **Export USFM** under **Content**; **Articles** and **Note Templates** under **Resources**; text size and interface language under **View**.
- Your account menu.

articles.title: Saving and working offline
headings: The status marks in the top bar
When two people edit the same thing
articles.body:
Your work is safe if you follow one rule: **notes, questions and articles save only when you select Save** (or **Save & Approve**). While you type, the text is also kept in your browser as a draft. This page explains where your work goes and what the status marks in the top bar mean.

![The top bar of the Notes screen with the save status at the right](/help/en/notes-1.png)

## Where your work goes
1. You type. The text is kept in your browser right away.
2. You select **Save**. The edit goes into a queue in your browser, then to the app's database. This does not touch Door43.
3. Once a night, the app publishes the approved content to Door43. If that step fails, your edits stay safe in the app's database and the next night catches up.

## The status marks in the top bar
- **saved**: everything is on the server.
- **saving N**: N edits are being sent.
- **N unsaved**: you have text that you typed but did not save. Select the mark to see the list and jump to each one. You can also discard one there.
- **offline** or **reconnecting…**, with **N queued**: there is no connection. See below.
- **N conflicts** or **N failed**: something needs your attention. See below.

If you try to close the tab or reload with unsaved text, the browser warns you. Unsaved text comes back when you return to the same note, question or article.

## Work offline
You can keep working when the connection drops. Each time you select **Save**, the edit is added to the queue and the mark shows **N queued — offline**. When the connection comes back, the queue is sent in order, and nothing is lost if you close the tab meanwhile.

If your sign-in expires, a message says **Your session expired — sign in to keep saving**. Select **Sign in**. The queued edits are sent after you sign in. Do not clear your browser data while edits are queued.

## When two people edit the same thing
If someone else saved the same note or question before you, the server refuses your edit, so you do not overwrite their work.
- On the [Notes](#help:notes) and [Questions](#help:questions) screens, a banner says that your version was not saved. Select **Reload note** (or **Reload question**) to load their version, then redo your change.
- In the top bar, a conflict shows as **N conflicts**. A panel in the bottom corner has **resolve N conflict(s)**. It sends your edit again on top of the current server version, so your edit wins. Use it only when you are sure.
- In the [Review queue](#help:review-queue), a window **Someone else saved this note first** lets you choose **Keep mine** or **Keep theirs**.

## When a save fails
**N failed** means an edit could not be accepted. The panel in the bottom corner lists it. Select **retry this edit**. If it still fails, select **discard this edit**. The confirmation window has **copy edit**, so you can copy the text first. Discarding deletes the edit from your device for good.

## Publishing to Door43
The nightly publish sends **approved** notes and questions. Rows that are still drafts or edited but not approved are held back, and Door43 keeps their last published text. An admin can also publish one book at any time from its package. See [Books](#help:books).

articles.title: Review queue
articles.body:
The **Review queue** is a work screen for the notes and questions of one chapter. You read each item, fix it, and approve it. It is also where you can add, move, trash and restore notes and see an item's history. Only approved items are published to Door43.

![The review queue for Obadiah 1 with the queue rail and the work card](/help/en/review-1.png)

## Open it
This screen has no button in the menus yet. Open it by its address: add `#/review/OBA/1` (book and chapter) after the app's address.

The top bar of this screen has no book or chapter controls. To leave, use the **More** menu (**Import from Door43** goes to Books) or change the address.

## Find an item
1. Choose **Notes** or **Questions** at the top of the queue.
2. Use the **Filter** area: **All statuses**, **Pending**, **Approved**, or (for notes) **Trashed**. For notes you can also filter by type (**All types**).
3. Select an item in the rail. On a phone, use the arrows and the count to go from card to card.

Each item has a chip for its state.

## Review and approve one note
1. Edit the **Quote**, the support reference and the note text in the work card.
2. Select **Save** to keep your changes. Select **Approve** to approve the item. A note that has never had an AI draft cannot be approved yet.
3. To approve many at once, select **Approve all notes (N)** (or **Approve all questions (N)**) above the queue. If some fail, the message tells you which one failed first. AI drafts nobody changed that are approved this way are not used as AI examples, because nobody read them one by one. Items someone edited still count. To make an unchanged draft count, approve it on its own. Approvals made with Approve all before this change still count.

More tools on a note card:
- **✨ Suggest** asks the AI for a draft. The draft goes into the editor. Select **Save** to keep it. It needs a quote and a support reference.
- **Template** inserts a curated template for the note's support reference.
- **Preserve** marks the note to survive future AI runs. **Hint** sends it to the next AI run as a hint.
- **Trash** moves a note to the trash. **Restore** brings it back, but only until the nightly publish: that night the trash is emptied and its notes are deleted for good. A note you set aside with **Not needed** on the Notes screen is in the trash too.
- **History** shows earlier versions of the item, and lets you restore one.
- **Retarget** moves the note to another verse of the chapter.
- **Move up**, **Move down** and **Insert note after this one** change the order. **+ Note** and **+ Question** add new ones.

Questions can be shown as cards (**Card view**) or in a table (**Grid view**). A question is deleted for good with **Delete**. There is no trash for questions.

## Look at the verse
The panel **This verse** is read-only context: the verse text and the word links. On a phone it opens as a sheet.

## Good to know
- If someone else saved the item first, a window offers **Keep mine** or **Keep theirs**. See [Saving and working offline](#help:save-and-sync).
- While an AI run holds the chapter, some changes are refused. The screen says which.

articles.title: Setting up the project (admin)
headings: If the project already has text
articles.body:
Setup tells the app where your project's text comes from and where your team's work is saved. Only an admin can open it. It has three parts: the **Setup wizard**, **Source overrides (advanced)**, and **Localization**. Door43 is the git server where unfoldingWord resources are published.

![The Setup page with the setup wizard on the first step](/help/en/admin-setup-1.png)

One database serves one organization. You cannot change the organization here. To use a different organization, press **Switch workspace…** at the bottom of the wizard panel. This switches the workspace and reloads the app.

## Run the setup wizard
1. Open **Setup** in the admin menu.
2. **Your organization:** check the organization and the **Resource language**. This is the language of the text and notes you produce. It is filled in from your organization's files when possible. Press **Next**.
3. **Sources to pull from:** set the **Default upstream org**. This is the organization you translate from. The default is unfoldingWord. Each resource is checked by default: **Literal text (GLT)**, **Simplified text (GST)**, translationNotes, translationQuestions, translationWords Links, translationWords and translationAcademy. Clear a check to choose **Leave blank** or **Use a different source**. For a different source, paste a **Door43 source URL**. Press **Next** when the sources are verified.
4. **Your scripture lanes:** a lane is one of your two scripture texts, literal or simplified. For each lane, confirm the **Target repository**. This is your organization's repository, and the editor saves your work there. Then answer **What are translators doing in this lane?** Choose **Editing the text** or **Aligning only**. Check **Upstream for this lane**. Press **Next**.
5. **Review & apply:** read the summary of where the app pulls from and where it saves. Fix any warning shown. Press **Apply configuration**.
6. **Done:** press **Go to Import** to bring in your first book (see [Books](#help:books)), or **Open the editor**.

## If the project already has text
The target repository of a lane is locked once the project holds text. To change the scripture source of such a lane, use **Change scripture source** in Preferences (see [Preferences](#help:preferences)). The wizard cannot do that.

## Source overrides (advanced)
An override makes one book take its notes or questions from a different Door43 repository. A book override wins over the project source.
1. Choose the **Book**.
2. Under **Add override**, choose the **Resource**: **Notes (tN)** or **Questions (tQ)**.
3. Choose the source, or choose **Other Door43 repo…** and paste a **Door43 repo URL**.
4. To limit the override to some chapters, fill **from ch** and **to ch**. Leave both empty for the whole book.
5. Press **Add override**. Use **Remove** to delete an override.

Set an override before the book's first import so it applies at once. A book that is already imported needs a full re-import to use a new override.

## Localization
This section edits the interface strings of your workspace.

articles.title: Managing the team and roles (admin)
headings: Change a role or remove someone
articles.body:
**Team & roles** shows who can use this workspace and what each person may do. Only an admin can open it.

![The Team & roles page with the People table](/help/en/admin-team-1.png)

There are three kinds of access:
- **Admin** can do everything an editor can. An admin can also open Setup and manage people.
- **Editor** can write content in the whole workspace: scripture, notes, words and questions. An editor cannot open Setup or manage people.
- **Viewer** can only read. Members of your Door43 organization who have no role here sign in as viewers.

Door43 is the git server where your organization's resources live. Its teams decide most roles: a person's Door43 team sets the role each time they sign in.

## See who has access
1. Open **Team & roles** in the admin menu.
2. Read the **People** table. Columns are **Person**, **Role**, **Source of role** and **Actions**.
3. **Source of role** is either **Door43 team** or **Manual grant**.
4. Click a row to see what that role can do.

## Add a person
1. In **Add a person**, type the **Door43 username**.
2. Choose the **Role**.
3. Press **Add**. If the username cannot be checked on Door43, the person is still added, with a note.

## Change a role or remove someone
1. Click the **Role** chip of a person to switch between admin and editor.
2. Press **Remove** to take away a manual role.
3. A change to a person whose role comes from a Door43 team lasts only until their next sign-in. Then the team sets the role again. To make it permanent, change their team on Door43.
4. The last admin cannot be demoted or removed. Someone must stay admin.

## Clear all manual roles
Press **Purge manual grants…** and confirm with **Purge**. This removes every manually granted role. Roles that come from a Door43 team are kept, and at least one admin always stays.

## Compare with Door43
**Door43 org roster** is a live, read-only list of the organization on Door43. It never changes a role. The **Access here** column shows what each member gets in this app. If Door43 cannot be read, the page says the list may be incomplete. An empty list then does not mean the organization has no members.

articles.title: Workflow, scripture source and publishing (admin)
articles.body:
**Workflow** shows how a book moves from draft to publish and gives you controls for the scripture text and for publishing. Only an admin can open it.

![The Workflow page with its four panels](/help/en/admin-workflow-1.png)

The page has four panels.

## The 8 steps
This panel is a description only, marked **Descriptive**. It lists the steps: **Draft**, **Peer check**, **Source check**, **Align**, **Translate resources**, **Harmonize**, **Final validation**, **Publish**. The app does not track which step a book is on, so there are no counts.

## AI pipeline
A pipeline job is one AI run for one chapter. This panel counts the jobs of the whole workspace: running, queued, paused, failed and done. It refreshes by itself every two minutes. Press **Refresh** to update now. Press **Open AI studio** to start or manage runs (see [AI studio](#help:admin-ai)).

## Scripture source
There is one card for the literal lane and one for the simplified lane. Each card shows the **Current source** and the **Export target**. It has two switches:
- **Text read-only** blocks new edits to the lane's scripture text.
- **Alignment writable** lets translators keep aligning words while the text is locked.

Click a switch to turn it on or off. The app asks you to confirm. The switches are locked while a source replacement is in progress.

### Activate a staged source
Starting a replacement happens on the Books screen's lane panel and in Preferences (see [Preferences](#help:preferences)). When a staged replacement is ready, its card says so.
1. Press **Activate…**.
2. Read the warning. After this, the lane reads from the new source and backing out means another replacement.
3. Tick **I understand translators will start reading the new source.**
4. Press **Activate**.

## Publishing
The nightly export writes the database to files and commits them to a branch on Door43. If automatic exports are not enabled on this deployment, the panel says so. The table lists past exports with **State**, **Rows**, **Branch** and **Committed**.

### Run an export now
1. Press **Run export now…**.
2. Choose the **Export scope**: **All books** or one book. Choose the **Resource**. You can enter **Chapters (optional)**, for example 13-14, when you chose one book and a tn, tq or twl resource.
3. Choose the **Door43 write mode**. **Merge with Door43** pulls Door43's current state first and keeps hand edits made on Door43 to rows you did not touch. **Overwrite Door43** skips that pull and needs a chapter range.
4. Press **Run export**. In overwrite mode this button reads **Overwrite Door43**.
5. Press **Check status** to follow the run.

A manual export takes several minutes and commits real files.

articles.title: Progress, review state, draft scorecard and suggestion inbox (admin)
headings: Set the review state of many rows
Check the quality of AI drafts
See which note kinds are marked Not needed
articles.body:
Four admin pages show and set how far the review has come. **Progress** shows the numbers. **Review state** changes the review state of many notes or questions at once. **Draft scorecard** shows how good the AI drafts of approved notes were. **Suggestion inbox** lists corrections editors keep making to those drafts. Only an admin can open them.

![The Progress page with totals and the book package board](/help/en/admin-progress-1.png)

## Read the Progress page
1. Open **Progress** in the admin menu.
2. The tiles at the top count the imported **Books**, **Verses**, **Notes**, **Word links** and **Questions**. **Approved** shows the share of notes, questions and verses that are approved, all together.
3. In **Book package board**, each row is one imported book. Click a row to see the same numbers for each chapter.
4. **Activity** lists the latest export runs and AI jobs.

The page loads each book one by one, so the tiles may say they are still loading.

## Set the review state of many rows
Use this when you already know the status of imported work. For example, a book was checked before it came into the app, so its notes should count as approved. For normal reviewing, see [Review queue](#help:review-queue).

![The Review state page with the Set review state form](/help/en/admin-progress-2.png)

1. Open **Review state** in the admin menu.
2. Under **Set review state**, choose the **Book** and the **Resource**: **Translation notes** or **Translation questions**.
3. Choose the **New state**: **Approved** or **Needs review**. **Needs review** puts the rows back in the review queue.
4. Choose **From chapter** and **To chapter**. Tick **Whole book** to use every chapter.
5. Press **Review change**. Nothing is saved yet. The app counts the rows it would change.
6. In **Confirm review state change**, check the book, chapters, resource, new state and **Rows to update**.
7. Press **Apply**, or **Cancel** to stop.

The message after saving tells you how many rows changed. The table **Current state by chapter** shows how many notes and questions are approved in each chapter.

Good to know:
- Every row in the range changes, including rows a translator is still working on.
- The text of the notes does not change. The change is recorded in the history as an admin action.
- These rows are not used as AI examples.
- If the app says the change could not be confirmed, it may be partly or fully applied. Check the counts in the table before you try again.

## Check the quality of AI drafts
**Draft scorecard** compares each approved translation note with the last AI draft of it, chapter by chapter. Use it to see whether a change to the AI's guidance makes drafts better. It changes nothing.

1. Open **Draft scorecard** in the admin menu.
2. Choose the **Book**. The table shows one row per chapter, and **Whole book** at the bottom.
3. Read the columns:
   - **Approved notes**: approved translation notes in the chapter. AI drafts nobody changed that were approved with **Approve all notes**, and notes approved by a review-state change, are left out, because nobody read them one by one. Approvals made with Approve all before this change are still counted.
   - **No draft logged**: notes with no AI draft on record. Edit history older than 180 days can be cleared.
   - **Draft was English**: the AI draft was the English note, not translated. These notes are left out of the columns to the right. A note that is the same as the English for a good reason, such as one that holds only links, is counted here too.
   - **Compared**: the notes the other columns are about.
   - **Approved unchanged**: the share approved exactly as the AI wrote them.
   - **Median similarity**: how much of a draft was kept, from 0 (all rewritten) to 1 (unchanged). When the changed part of a note is longer than 2,000 characters, only its first 2,000 characters are compared, so that note's similarity is approximate and the chapter's median is marked ≈. Point at the ≈ to see how many notes it covers.
   - **Period added after ]**: of the drafts that end with ] and no period, the share where the editor had to add the period.
   - **Context pack**: the version of the guidance the AI was given, with how many notes used it. Hover over it to see the full name. **Not pinned (latest pack at run time, if any)** means the run was not tied to one version: it used the latest guidance when it ran, or none if no guidance had been exported yet. **Run not on record** means the AI run has been cleared. Each draft is matched to its AI run by time, so in rare cases where runs overlapped a draft can be credited to the wrong run.

If the English notes cannot be read for some chapters, a message names those chapters and gives each reason. No draft in them is left out as English, and their counts are marked with *. On the **Whole book** row, * means only part of the book was checked.

## Turn repeated corrections into guidance
**Suggestion inbox** finds corrections editors made again and again to the AI's translation-note drafts, so you can fix them once. For example, editors may add a period after the final ] of almost every note, or delete a tag the AI keeps adding.

1. Open **Suggestion inbox** in the admin menu.
2. Choose the **Book**. The app works the cards out now, from that book's approved notes (the same notes as **Draft scorecard**). There is no nightly run, so a large book can take a few seconds.
3. Each card shows:
   - the change: the AI's words, then the approved words (**deleted** when the editors removed them). **at the end of the note** means the change was made only at the very end.
   - **Made in X of Y drafts that had it**: X notes had this change made. Y drafts contained the words it changes, including those X.
   - **Chapters**: where the change was made.
   - **Suggested home**: where the fix belongs. **House-style rule** is offered only for three kinds of change that are safe in every note: the period after a final ], deleting a tag in parentheses or brackets such as (مُكيَّف), and changing only the marks (vowels, tanween) on one word. The rule is tried on every draft of the book: the card says "the rule would change N drafts in this book; it matches the editor's change in M (P%)". It is offered only when it changes at least 10 drafts and gives exactly the approved text in at least 8 of every 10 (9 of 10 for marks). It must also give exactly the approved text on each of the card's examples; when it does not, the card says "the rule doesn't reproduce the editor's change on every example". In a large book some drafts may take too long to check. Then the card says how many could not be checked, and when the drafts that were checked would pass, it says the rule "could not be fully checked in time". The rule is not offered while any draft is unchecked. The card also says what kind of rule it would create. **Note template** is for words that come from a template. **Term** is for a change of one to three words. Everything else is a **Common issues line**.
   - three examples: the AI draft and the approved note around the change.
4. Choose what to do:
   - **Approve** on a house-style card asks you to confirm, then adds the rule to [Style: House style](#help:admin-style), switched on. It changes every AI draft that arrives after that, in every book, for notes and for questions and answers. Its examples there are real lines from the drafts.
   - **Approve** on any other card copies a line for you. The term, template and Common issues editors cannot be filled in from here, so open the editor with the button and paste the line.
   - **Reject** hides the card for good, in every book.

A card appears only when the same change was made in at least 10 notes across at least 3 chapters. Spaces and line breaks are ignored, and changes inside a bold Scripture quote and rewrites longer than a few words are left out. A change is not shown when a house-style rule already makes it (even a rule that is switched off), a term already gives the approved words, a template already contains them, or the Common issues text already lists them. A card you sent to another editor goes away once that editor's text covers it. If it still shows after your edit, reject it.

## See which note kinds are marked Not needed
Below the cards, **Note kinds marked Not needed** lists the kinds of translation notes (the translationAcademy article a note points to, such as figs-yousingular) that editors keep marking **Not needed**. It counts all books, not only the one you chose. It only informs you: it does not switch any kind off.

- A kind is listed when at least 10 of its notes, in at least 3 chapters, were marked **Not needed** in the last 30 days. A note still counts after the nightly export removes it for good. A note that was restored does not count.
- Each card shows the kind, how many notes were marked, in how many chapters, and which books.
- **Dismiss** hides the kind from this list for good.

articles.title: AI studio and AI service (admin)
headings: Let the team ask the AI help assistant
Let editors ask the assistant for bulk edits
articles.body:
**AI studio** is where you have AI translate a chapter's translation notes or translation questions, and where you save the AI provider key of your organization. A **Translate chapter** or **Translate questions** run locks parts of its chapter while it is starting, running or paused, but a run still waiting in line locks nothing, and neither do **Import from Door43**, **Pull Aquifer drafts** and **Re-source notes from English**. The [Scripture](#help:scripture), [Notes](#help:notes) and [Questions](#help:questions) articles say exactly what is locked on each screen.

![The AI studio with the run controls and the runs table](/help/en/admin-ai-1.png)

## Start an AI run
1. Open **AI studio** in the admin menu.
2. Choose the **Book** and type the **Chapter**.
3. Press **AI** and choose **Translate chapter** (the chapter's translation notes) or **Translate questions** (its translation questions). These two appear only in a translation project, one that translates from a source language.
4. In the confirm window, choose a chapter or a range and press **Start**.

Only one job runs at a time. The other jobs wait in line. When AI drafts are ready, a banner on the page tells you to review them.

A run on a whole chapter does not redraft notes or questions that are already approved. It keeps them as they are, and when the run ends a banner lists them. To get a new AI draft for one approved note or question, run the AI on that one alone (for a note, **Redo** on the note). If the AI returns a note unchanged from the English, that draft is not applied: the note keeps its text, and a banner lists it.

The same **AI** menu also has **Import from Door43**. Admins on a translation project also see **Pull Aquifer drafts** and **Re-source notes from English**. Re-sourcing replaces the book from Door43 and discards local edits, so the app asks you to confirm.

AI runs are only for translation projects. In a source project, one that does not translate from another language (such as unfoldingWord's English), the page says so under its title, and the button reads **Import** instead of **AI**. Choose a **Book**, then press **Import**: it opens **Import from Door43** straight away, with no menu. The **Book** list holds only books already in the project, and this import updates chapters of that book from Door43. To bring in a new book, use **Bring in OBA…** (with your book's code) on the **Books** screen; see [Books and the book package](#help:books). The same import is on a book's package and on the Scripture, Notes and Questions screens, as the download icon in their top bar. On a phone those screens move it into your account menu, as the item **Import from Door43**.

## Follow the runs
The table **Runs — this workspace** shows **Type**, **Scope**, **State**, **Progress**, **Started** and **Requested by**. Runs started by other people are read-only. For your own runs you can press **Cancel** while a run is still queued. A failed **Translate** run shows **Retry** greyed out, because it cannot be retried here: start a new run instead. Runs of the older AI actions, such as **Write translation notes**, stay in the list under their names, but those actions are no longer offered and their runs have no **Retry**. Press **Dismiss** to hide a failed, cancelled or finished run, or **Dismiss all** to hide them all. **Refresh** updates the list.

If the page says **AI not configured**, the AI connection is not set up for this workspace. A technical administrator must set the BT_API_TOKEN setting on the server. Until then retrying is not available.

## Save your own AI key
The section **AI service** sets which AI provider runs your pipeline jobs.
1. Choose the **Provider**: Google Gemini, xAI Grok, Claude (API) or OpenAI.
2. Choose the **Model**.
3. Type your **API key**.
4. Press **Save**.

Once saved, the key is stored encrypted and is never shown again. You see **Configured** with the last characters of the key. Press **Replace** to enter a new key, or **Clear** to remove it. If a red or yellow notice says bringing your own key is not enabled on this deployment, a technical administrator must enable it first.

## Let the team ask the AI help assistant
Under the key settings, the switch **Let team members ask the AI help assistant** turns on the **Ask AI** area in the Help panel for everyone in your organization. It is off until you turn it on. The assistant uses your organization's AI key, so it only answers once an API key is saved. Each person can use up to a daily dollar amount, shown under the switch. Turn the switch off at any time to hide **Ask AI** again.

## Let editors ask the assistant for bulk edits
Next to that switch, **Let editors ask an AI assistant to propose bulk edits** turns on the **Assistant** chat on the Rapid check notes screen, for editors and admins. It is off until you turn it on. It uses your organization's AI key and only answers once an API key is saved. It proposes changes, and nothing is saved until the person presses **Apply**. Each person can use up to a daily dollar amount, shown under the switch.

articles.title: Teaching the AI your style (admin)
headings: House style: fixes made to AI drafts
Lessons: what the AI learns from editor corrections
Pin, delete, or move a lesson to Common issues
See who changed the preferences, and undo a change
articles.body:
**Style** holds what the AI is told before it drafts anything for your project: who the readers are, how to write, which terms to use. Together this is the context pack. Every AI draft is written against it. Only an admin can save changes.

![The Style page with the section list and the context pack bar](/help/en/admin-style-1.png)

The bar at the top shows the state of the context pack, for example **Context pack ready**, with counts of terms and examples. **Export now** builds a new pack. The switch **Project mode** shows whether the project is in translation or authoring mode. The sections below apply to translation projects only. In other projects the page says so.

## Fill in the sections
Use the list on the left to jump to a section. After you change a section, press **Save**. Until you do, the text you typed in **Brief**, **Instructions** or **Common issues** is kept in this browser, even if you reload the page, and is counted as unsaved at the top of the page.

- **Brief:** fill in **Audience**, **Purpose**, **Register** and **Script / direction notes**. Register is how formal the drafts should be: **Default (auto)**, **Formal** or **Informal**.
- **Instructions:** free text (Markdown) added to every AI drafting and checking request. Use **Preview** to see how it looks.
- **Common issues:** free text about problems that reviewers flag again and again.
- **Terminology:** your decisions about terms. You can give a preferred rendering, mark a term as forbidden with what to use instead, or mark it do-not-translate. This section can also import and export a CSV file. Deleting a term shows **Term deleted** with **Undo** for a few seconds; click **Undo** to bring the same term back. If the project has since gained the same term, or someone changed it, the term stays deleted and a message says why. If the server could not be reached, the message says **Try again** and **Undo** stays available.
- **Examples:** notes and questions that were approved in the editor one at a time, or checked and approved in **Rapid check**. The AI sees them as models of good work. AI drafts nobody changed that were approved with **Approve all notes** or **Approve all questions**, and items approved by an admin's review-state change, are not examples. Approvals made with Approve all before this change still count. Switch between **Notes** and **Questions**. Press **Revoke** to remove an example. Revoking returns the item to the edited state.
- **QA rules** and **Templates:** QA rules are listed with **Coming soon**. **Templates** shows how many note templates are translated. Press **Open template curation →** to work on them (see [Note templates](#help:admin-templates)).

## House style: fixes made to AI drafts
**House style** lists small fixes the app makes to every AI translation draft when the draft arrives, so editors do not have to make the same correction on every note. They apply to notes and to questions and their answers. For example, a rule can add the closing period after an alternate translation in brackets, or delete a tag the AI keeps adding.

- Each rule shows what it fixes (**Before** and **After**) and what it leaves alone.
- Every rule the development team adds is **Off** until an admin switches it **On**. Switch a rule on only after the language's editor has confirmed it. A rule made by approving a card in the [suggestion inbox](#help:admin-progress) starts **On**.
- A rule changes drafts that arrive after you switch it on. Drafts already in the project stay as they are.
- Scripture quotes in bold and the Quote column are never changed.
- The closing-period rule adds nothing when the words inside the final brackets already end with a punctuation mark (… ؟ . ! ? or ؛, so ... too), so the rule never adds a second mark.
- The AI's original wording is saved with each draft's record, so the fixes can be checked later.
- If a draft still contains the English phrase "If it would be helpful in your language", the app notes this in the draft's record for later review. It does not rewrite the phrase, and nothing on screen shows this yet.

You cannot add or edit rules on this page. New rules are added by the development team, or by approving a card in the suggestion inbox.

## Lessons: what the AI learns from editor corrections
**Lessons** is a short list the AI is given with every new draft. Each night, the app reads what editors changed in the AI drafts they approved and writes the list from those changes. Each lesson says what to do, with one example (**AI wrote** and **Editor wrote**) and the number of notes it was seen in.

Lessons are **Off** for every project until an admin turns them on. While they are off, the page says so: the AI is NOT learning from editor corrections, and new drafts get only the sections above. Turn lessons on when your editors have approved enough notes, for example after a few weeks of work.

- On a night with new approvals, the app compares the AI draft with the approved note for the notes that count as examples (see **Examples** above), in the 2 most recently approved chapters, plus any chapter an earlier stopped run left waiting. If there are more notes than it can compare in one night, the next night finishes the same chapters first, even if editors have moved on to other chapters, and the newest chapters come after that.
- The app calls your AI service once on a night that found corrections to learn from. Your project's AI account pays for it. The page shows the last run, what happened, and about what it cost.
